#set working directory
```{R}

setwd("/Users/sterlingbutler/Desktop/RICA_FILES_03262025")

#import the feature table using the read_q2biom()
asv<- read_q2biom("table.biom")

#import the taxa file as a qiime2 artifact and then convert it into a usable tax table for phyloseq
tax <- read_qza("taxonomy.qza")
taxa <- tax$data %>% as_tibble() %>% 
  separate(Taxon, sep=";", c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")) %>% 
  select(-Confidence) %>% arrange(Feature.ID) %>% mutate(ASV = 1:n()) %>% 
  mutate(newcol = "ASV") %>%
  unite("ASVs", newcol:ASV)

#make the taxa table into a data frame 
taxa<-as.data.frame(taxa)

#import the meta data
meta_df<-read.csv("qiime2_08022024_16S_RICA_META.csv") %>%
  mutate(spiro_timepoint = paste(structural_zero_spiro, Time_Point, sep = "_") )
  
  

```

```{R}
#make the correct column names for the phyloseq object 
taxa1 = taxa %>% tibble::column_to_rownames("Feature.ID")
meta = meta_df %>% tibble::column_to_rownames("sample")

#convert the taxa table back into a matrix, so phyloseq can read
tax_mat = as.matrix(taxa1)

#make the individual phyloseq objects otu_table, tax_table, sample_data
otu<-otu_table(asv, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
tax_table<-tax_table(tax_mat)
sample<-sample_data(meta)

```


```{R}
#Check to see if the labels for samples and ASVs for the different 
sample_names(sample)
sample_names(otu)
ntaxa(tax_table)
head(taxa_names(tax_table))

```

```{R}

#lets make that phyloseq object now
phy= phyloseq(otu, tax_table, sample)

#remove Mitochondria/ chloroplast
phy <- phy %>% subset_taxa( Family!= "Mitochondria" | is.na(Family) & Class!="Chloroplast" | is.na(Class) ) 

#remove NTC and a sample with 20 total reads 
phy <-phy %>% subset_samples(Species!="NA")
phy <-phy %>% subset_samples(Bag_Number!="32")

#filter out the noise in the data, this filters out any taxa that have counts less than 5
phy_fill= filter_taxa(phy , function(x) sum(x > 5) > (0.05*length(x)), TRUE)

## Basic summary information for the phyloseq object that you just created
#number of taxa
ntaxa(phy_fill)
#number of samples
nsamples(phy_fill)
#number of variables
sample_variables(phy_fill)

```

```{R}

#Use tax_fix() on your phyloseq data with default arguments to repair most tax_table problems (missing or uninformative values)
phy_fill <- tax_fix(phy_fill)

```



```{R}

#test the if groups are different 
set.seed(1)
phy_clr = microbiome::transform(phy_fill, 'clr')

pairwise.adonis(t(otu_table(phy_clr)), sample_data(phy_clr)$Time_Point, sim.method = "euclidean",
                p.adjust.m = "bonferroni")

pairwise.adonis(t(otu_table(phy_clr)), sample_data(phy_clr)$structural_zero_spiro, sim.method = "euclidean",
                p.adjust.m = "bonferroni")

pairwise.adonis(t(otu_table(phy_clr)), sample_data(phy_clr)$spiro_timepoint, sim.method = "euclidean",
                p.adjust.m = "bonferroni")

#beta dispersion
dist_clr <- dist(t(otu_table(phy_clr)), method = "euclidean")
group <- sample_data(phy_clr)$spiro_timepoint

disp <- betadisper(dist_clr, group)
disp
permutest(disp, pairwise = TRUE)

```
```{R}
my_comparisons = list( c("No_T2", "Yes_T2"), c("No_T2", "No_T1"), c("No_T2", "Yes_T1"), c("No_T1", "Yes_T1"), 
                       c("No_T1", "Yes_T2"), c("Yes_T1", "Yes_T2"))

# Compute dissimilarity indices
#dissimilarity_indices <- vegdist(otu_table(t(ps_merge_clr)), method = "euclidean")

# PERMDISP2 procedure for multivariate homogeneity of group dispersions
#model <- betadisper(dissimilarity_indices, sample_data(ps_merge)$Site.Status)

# Convert distances to a data frame
distances_df <- as.data.frame(disp$distances)

# Combine with sample data
combined_df <- cbind(sample_data(phy_clr), distances_df) 

dispersion_plot <- ggplot(combined_df, aes(x = spiro_timepoint, y = disp$distances)) +
  geom_violin(aes(fill = spiro_timepoint)) +
  #stat_summary(
 #   fun = median,
 #   geom = 'line',
 #   linetype = "dashed",
#    aes(group = Species_sample, color = Species_sample)
#  ) +
  guides(group = guide_legend(order = 0),
         color = guide_legend(order = 1)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.1) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Time_Point), position = position_dodge(width = 0.1), size = 1) +
 scale_color_manual(values = c("black", "red"  )) +  # Assign different shapes
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#5E738F","gray80", "#006700","green")) +
  theme_classic2() +
  theme_linedraw() +
  ylab("Distance to Centroid") +
  theme_classic2()+
  theme(
    legend.text = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 7),
    legend.key.height = unit(0.2, 'cm'),
    legend.key.width = unit(0.2, 'cm'),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size= 20, colour = "white"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
  legend.position = "right") +
 guides(fill = guide_legend(title = "Spiro SZ + Time Point", nrow=4),
  color = guide_legend(title = "Time Point", nrow=3)
   ) +
  
 stat_compare_means(comparisons = my_comparisons, 
                   # label.y = c(119, 123.5, 130), 
                    aes(label = after_stat(p.signif)))

dispersion_plot


```

```{R}

#PCOA with time point as shape, genotype as color

drive_tax_pca <- phy_fill %>%
  tax_transform("clr", rank = "Genus") %>%
  # when no distance matrix or constraints are supplied, PCA is the default/auto ordination method
  ord_calc(method = "PCA") %>%
  ord_plot(axes = c(1, 2),color = "Genotype", shape="Time_Point", size=2.9,
           plot_taxa = 1:3, size = 2,
           tax_lab_style = tax_lab_style(size = 2, alpha = 0.5))+
  scale_colour_manual(values=c("#56B4E9","#CBD588","#5F7FC7", "darkorchid","#DA5724","#CD9BCD","#006700","yellow2",
                               "gray80", "#AD6F3B", "#673770","#8569D5", 
                               "#5E738F","#D1A33D", "orange","#ff6700","aquamarine4", "#652926",
                               "lightblue4", "lightpink","royalblue4","#D14285",
                               "palevioletred1", "#56B4E9","#CBD588", "#5F7FC7","#DA5724",
                               "#CD9BCD", "gray80", "darkorchid",
                               "#AD6F3B", "#673770","#D14285", "#652926"))+ 
  theme_classic2()

drive_tax_pca

ggsave("drive_taxa_pca.png", width = 10, height = 5)

```


```{R}

pca <- phy_fill %>%
  tax_transform("clr", rank = "Genus") %>%
  # when no distance matrix or constraints are supplied, PCA is the default/auto ordination method
  ord_calc(method = "PCA") %>%
  ord_plot(axes = c(1, 2),
           color = "Time_Point", 
           auto_caption = NA,
           shape="structural_zero_spiro"
          #this lines of code will ad in the taxa bars over points 
            #,plot_taxa = 1:3, size = 2.9
           #,tax_lab_style = tax_lab_style(size = 3.4, alpha = 0.5)
           ) +
  labs(
    colour= "Spirochaetaceae SZ + Time Point",
    shape = "Spirochaetaceae SZ")+ 
 theme_classic2()+
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9),
     axis.title.y = element_text(size = 9),
     axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
     axis.text.x = element_text(size = 9)
  ) +
 scale_color_manual(values = c( "#5E738F","gray80","black", "red", "#006700","green"))+
  stat_ellipse(aes(colour = spiro_timepoint), linewidth = 1)
  

?stat_ellipse
pca
```
